title: Ops Lab: Ephemeral Microflow Runner for Safe Admin Playflows
creator: Ava Guo
description:
Goal: build a lightweight, developer-friendly 'Ops Lab' microflow runner that executes admin playbook steps as ephemeral, auditable tasks inside a sandboxed environment. The runner is intended to let SREs and support engineers rehearse incident remediation and validate runbook changes without touching production resources. Key properties:

- Ephemeral execution contexts: each microflow runs with short-lived, scoped credentials and an isolated namespace that mirrors customer-facing resources.
- Dry-run & validation pass: a preflight validator executes syntactic and semantic checks (idempotency, required approvals, policy whitelists) and reports mismatches.
- Policy gating & safety validators: RBAC and risk heuristics are enforced before steps can reach a production agent; high-risk steps require an explicit approval flow.
- Step-level telemetry & rollback: every step emits structured telemetry, and the runner supports automatic compensating actions on failure.
- Event-triggered playback: microflows can be bound to alerts or a replay queue for simulated incident drills.
- Audit-first design: immutable audit events, integrated with the audit log pipeline and KMS-backed proof of origin.
- Minimal local dev surface: a CLI shim + containerized sandbox for engineers to iterate on microflows locally.

Non-goals: full migration of existing runbook inventory in this ticket; we aim to provide a safe launcher and catalog adapter for subsequent onboarding tasks.
updates: 2026-02-27: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Platform and Security. Agreed on core invariants (ephemeral creds, audit trail, and preflight safety). Action: security to draft RBAC mappings.

2026-03-03: Prototype CLI that can execute a 3-step microflow against a containerized sandbox. Demo recorded and uploaded to internal demo page. Observed 12% latency overhead vs direct tooling, acceptable for sandbox usage.

2026-03-06: Design review with Product and Design. Decided to reuse existing runbook DSL (yaml-first) and extend with 'safety:level' and 'compensate' fields. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/ephemeral-microflow-runner

2026-03-09: Implemented preflight validator (PR open). Validator checks: syntax, idempotency heuristics, resource-scope, and a simple risk score. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runner/pull/4392

2026-03-11: Integration tests: simulated incident replay (5 runs) — successful dry-run validations (5/5), sandbox execution success 4/5 due to a timing race in the ephemeral token refresh. Patch to token manager in review.
2026-03-13: Security flagged a blocker: mappings for on-prem operator agents require a formal KMS usage review and SSO lookup flow. Security review requested (ticket attached).
2026-03-14: Decision: ship an MVP for hosted sandbox first; on-prem agent work will be a follow-up dependent on security signoff. Added explicit feature flag for RBAC enforcement toggles.
